calls.head: A shadow job for Protas, Dubois and Wilson
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Dubois and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Panthers’ first line is B. Tkachuk, Bennett and M. Tkachuk.

calls.body: The Panthers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Capitals’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Capitals more than most. The Capitals take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.head: Picky vs. Trigger-happy
calls.body: The Capitals wait for good looks, but the Panthers settle for hopeful ones. Washington is the league’s best for shot quality, and Florida is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should be the Capitals’.

surprises.head: Washington hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Washington’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 27, against their usual 96 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Washington flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Florida allows fewer shots than almost anyone. Not tonight: Washington took 48 of the 78 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Washington would expect about 45%. A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

story.head: The Capitals edge the Panthers
paras: Jack St. Ivany, in his 62nd NHL game, scored his first NHL goal early in the first to open the scoring for the Capitals. Brady Tkachuk made it 1-1 for Florida 52 seconds later. The Panthers’ Sandis Vilmanis left in the first period and didn’t return. Brady Tkachuk struck again on the power play midway through the period to put the Panthers ahead 2-1. Alex Tuch tied it 2-2 for Washington early in the second, and Aliaksei Protas put the Capitals ahead for good midway through the period. Pierre-Luc Dubois made it 4-2 early in the third, and that one stood up as the winner. With the goalie pulled and 47 seconds left, Sam Bennett pulled the Panthers within one, but the Capitals held on. The Panthers’ Matthew Tkachuk finished with three assists.
The Capitals had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Panthers 23-14 at 5-on-5. Logan Thompson made 27 saves for the Caps, and Akira Schmid stopped 27 of 31 at the other end.

Tom Wilson was thrown out with a five-minute major for boarding and a game misconduct midway through the first. The Capitals moved to 9-6-0, fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Panthers fell to 9-6-2, fifth in the Atlantic.
